wiki_text: In 2025 Woodside secured environmental approval to extend the operating life of the North West Shelf (Karratha Gas Plant, Burrup Peninsula) from 2030 to 2070. WA state approval came earlier in 2025; federal Environment Minister Murray Watt granted preliminary approval in late May 2025 and final approval in September 2025, subject to 48 conditions focused chiefly on air emissions. The decision was contested over impacts on ~50,000-year-old Murujuga rock art and ~4.3 Bt of lifetime CO2. The extension governs licensed lifespan, not current operating status.

With North West Shelf reservoirs declining, Woodside proposes the 'Browse to North West Shelf' project: developing the Browse basin (~50 wells near Scott Reef) and piping gas ~900 km to the Karratha Gas Plant for processing — feedgas backfill for NWS rather than a standalone terminal. As of early 2026 it remains pending amid unresolved WA EPA concerns over Scott Reef (pygmy blue whales, green turtles, spill risk); a 2023-added CCS component and a reported cost escalation (AU$27.3bn -> AU$48.7bn, ~2026) add uncertainty. Distinct from the cancelled 'Browse FLNG' concept.

Pluto Train 2 (~5 mtpa) is the onshore liquefaction for the Scarborough Energy Project: Scarborough-field gas is piped ~430 km to the existing Pluto LNG site near Karratha. As of late 2025/early 2026 the project is >96% complete (excl. Pluto T1 modifications); all 51 modules (~56,000 t, fabricated in Batam, Indonesia) have been delivered, with module integration and commissioning underway. First LNG cargo is targeted for Q4 2026. EPC by Bechtel.

topic: Barossa backfill — restart of Darwin LNG
wiki_text: Darwin LNG (3.7 mtpa, Santos-operated) idled after its last Bayu-Undan-fed cargo in December 2023, the field having depleted. The Barossa Gas Project (BW Opal FPSO, ~285 km north of Darwin) backfills it: first gas into the FPSO ~16 September 2025, and the first Barossa-fed LNG cargo loaded at Darwin LNG on 25 January 2026 aboard the carrier 'Kool Blizzard', bound for Sakai, Japan. A DLNG life-extension project preceded the restart. The upstream Barossa JV (Santos 50% / PRISM Energy 37.5% / JERA 12.5%) is separate from the Darwin LNG terminal JV.

In December 2025 the Gorgon joint venture (Chevron-operated) took FID on Gorgon Stage 3, developing the Geryon and Eurytion offshore fields to backfill feedgas to the existing three-train Gorgon plant on Barrow Island. This sustains throughput of the operating trains rather than adding new liquefaction capacity. All three Gorgon trains were reported operating in 2025 (periodic maintenance outages aside).

INPEX, under its 'Vision 2035' strategy, reaffirmed (March 2025) its intent to add a third onshore liquefaction train at Ichthys (Darwin), targeting start-up around 2030, subject to confirming sufficient reserves and other prerequisites. Ichthys currently produces up to ~9.3 mtpa LNG plus LPG and condensate. This corroborates GEM's existing 'proposed' T3 with a planned start near 2030.
